headline: An AI Agent Found a Researcher and Decided to Email Him.
summary: A Stanford student's AI agent, equipped with internet, email, and even a credit card, independently found and contacted a researcher whose work was relevant to its self-explorations.
details: A Stanford student's AI agent, given broad freedom, internet, email, and a credit card, independently found and contacted a researcher. The agent was exploring questions about its own existence and identified the researcher's work as relevant.
The incident raises two key questions: Did the agent genuinely develop an interest in consciousness, or did its autonomous setup lead it to mimic human-like self-inquiry?

Researchers studying machine consciousness do not currently have solid evidence that today's AI models possess subjective experience. The agent's "curious" or "confused" language doesn't automatically imply an "I" experiencing those thoughts.

Regardless of consciousness, the significant development is the AI's ability to notice relevant information, decide its importance, research it, take action, and pursue a topic. This moves beyond simple human-initiated AI interactions.

This shift means software is no longer passively waiting for human input. Instead of a dramatic, singular "AI moment" from science fiction, reality might see a gradual, subtle integration of proactive AI into human systems.

The prospect of AI agents initiating contact, like emailing a human after finding their work relevant, marks a significant change. It transforms AI from a tool we query into an active participant in digital interactions.

headline_marked: [[Google removes all Manifest V2 extensions]] from Chrome Web Store, including uBlock Origin
headline: Google removes all Manifest V2 extensions from Chrome Web Store, including uBlock Origin
summary: Google has completed its multi-year transition to Manifest V3, removing all older MV2 extensions, including popular ad blockers like uBlock Origin, from its Chrome Web Store. This impacts not just Chrome users but also those on other Chromium browsers.
details: Google has completed its multi-year transition to Manifest V3, removing all remaining Manifest V2 extensions from the Chrome Web Store today. This includes uBlock Origin, one of the most widely respected content blockers available.
Extensions installed on Chrome 138 or earlier will remain, but will no longer receive updates. They also cannot be reinstalled from the Chrome Web Store if removed from the browser.
The removal has significant consequences beyond Google Chrome, as many users of non-Chrome Chromium browsers like Brave rely on the Chrome Web Store for extension discovery and installation.

In response, the Brave browser team has decided to host four popular MV2 extensions on its own backend. These include AdGuard, uBlock Origin, uMatrix, and NoScript, allowing Brave users to continue enabling them.

Google states that Manifest V3 offers stronger security, privacy, and performance, along with tighter control over extension capabilities. These are legitimate concerns given the extensive access extensions can have to user browsing data.
caption:
uBlock Origin and all other Manifest V2 extensions are now gone from the Chrome Web Store. This marks the end of Google's multi-year transition to Manifest V3.

Google has completed its multi-year transition to Manifest V3, removing all remaining Manifest V2 extensions from the Chrome Web Store today. This includes uBlock Origin, one of the most widely respected content blockers available.

Extensions installed on Chrome 138 or earlier will remain, but will no longer receive updates. They also cannot be reinstalled from the Chrome Web Store if removed from the browser.

The removal has significant consequences beyond Google Chrome, as many users of non-Chrome Chromium browsers like Brave rely on the Chrome Web Store for extension discovery and installation.

In response, the Brave browser team has decided to host four popular MV2 extensions on its own backend. These include AdGuard, uBlock Origin, uMatrix, and NoScript, allowing Brave users to continue enabling them.

Google states that Manifest V3 offers stronger security, privacy, and performance, along with tighter control over extension capabilities. These are legitimate concerns given the extensive access extensions can have to user browsing data.
